---
title: TaggedRedisDriver
description: "Tag-scoped proxy over RedisDriver for grouped cache invalidation via Redis sets."
---

<ApiBadge type="proxy" />
<ApiBadge type="cache" />
<ApiBadge type="redis" />
<ApiBadge type="tags" />
<ApiBadge type="bulk-invalidation" />

`Skim\Cache\TaggedRedisDriver` is a proxy returned by `Cache::tags()`. It wraps the RedisDriver and adds tag membership tracking via Redis sets. On `set()`, the key is SADD'd to each tag's set. On `flush()`, all member keys are deleted along with the tag sets themselves.

```txt
Symbol: Skim\Cache\TaggedRedisDriver
Source: src/Cache/TaggedRedisDriver.php
Lifecycle: created per Cache::tags() call, no persistent state beyond Redis sets
```

<CodeExample label="Basic usage" source="llm-generated">
```php
Cache::tags(['users'])->set('user:42:profile', $data, 3600);
Cache::tags(['users'])->flush(); // Deletes user:42:profile and all tagged keys
```
</CodeExample>

<WarningBox>

flush() is destructive — removes all keys associated with any constructor tag

</WarningBox>

<WarningBox>

Requires live Redis connection

</WarningBox>

## Architecture

Each tag maps to a Redis set at key `{prefix}tag:{tag_name}`. The set members are the full prefixed cache keys. flush() uses SMEMBERS + DEL, which is acceptable for tag-scoped invalidation at application scale.

<NoteBox>

Why Redis sets: O(1) membership check, atomic SADD, natural TTL via separate key expiry. This class does NOT implement the driver interface — it's a proxy with a reduced API (set, get, flush only).

</NoteBox>

## Read API

<ApiMethod name="get">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public function get(string $key, mixed $default = null): mixed
```

</ApiSignature>

Delegates directly to the underlying RedisDriver. Tags do not affect reads.

<ApiParam name="$key" type="string" required>

Cache key to read.

</ApiParam>

<ApiParam name="$default" type="mixed">

Fallback returned on miss.

</ApiParam>

</ApiMethod>

## Write API

<ApiMethod name="set">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public function set(string $key, mixed $value, ?int $ttl = null): bool
```

</ApiSignature>

Adds the prefixed key to each tag's Redis set via SADD, then delegates the write to the underlying RedisDriver.

<ApiParam name="$key" type="string" required>

Cache key to write.

</ApiParam>

<ApiParam name="$value" type="mixed" required>

Payload to persist.

</ApiParam>

<ApiParam name="$ttl" type="?int">

TTL in seconds, or null for no expiry.

</ApiParam>

</ApiMethod>

## Invalidation

<ApiMethod name="flush">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public function flush(): bool
```

</ApiSignature>

For each constructor tag, reads all member keys from the Redis set via SMEMBERS, deletes them, then deletes the tag set itself.

<CodeExample label="Basic usage" source="llm-generated">
```php
Cache::tags(['users', 'posts'])->flush(); // All keys tagged 'users' OR 'posts'
```
</CodeExample>

<WarningBox>

Destructive — removes all keys associated with any constructor tag

</WarningBox>

<WarningBox>

Deletes the tag sets themselves

</WarningBox>

</ApiMethod>
